_comment: One grammar point per unit, shown before the first lesson of that unit.
Hand-authored and deliberately narrow: a single rule the learner can hold in
mind while meeting the unit's vocabulary. Stress marks are combining acutes.
Keep each body to one or two sentences — this is a teaching card, not a chapter.
The ORDER is the point: spine notes run simple to complex in the sequence the
external courses agree on (docs/grammar-sequence.md), and a branch note never
uses a case or tense its chapter's spine has not yet introduced.

core1.title: No “a”, no “the”, no “is”
core1.body: Russian has no articles, and it leaves out the present tense of “to be”.

core2.title: Two verb patterns
core2.body: Most verbs follow either the -е- pattern (чита́ю, чита́ешь) or the -и- pattern (говорю́, говори́шь).

core3.title: Every noun has a gender
core3.body: A noun ending in a consonant is masculine, in -а/-я feminine, in -о/-е neuter. Everything that describes it must agree.

core4.title: Making things plural
core4.body: Masculine and feminine nouns usually take -ы or -и; neuter nouns take -а or -я. (A few masculine nouns take a stressed -а́ instead — дом → дома́ — and Around Town shows them.)

core5.title: Saying where something is
core5.body: After в or на meaning “in” or “on”, the noun takes the prepositional case, usually ending in -е.

core6.title: The accusative marks the object
core6.body: The thing an action is done to changes form. Feminine -а becomes -у; inanimate masculine looks unchanged.

core7.title: The past tense agrees with the subject
core7.body: Drop -ть and add -л, -ла, -ло or -ли. It matches gender and number, not person — “I read” differs for a man and a woman.

core8.title: Two aspects of every verb
core8.body: Imperfective verbs describe the process or a repeated action; perfective verbs describe one completed act.

core9.title: Talking about the future
core9.body: A perfective verb in its present-tense forms already means the future: я сде́лаю is “I will do”. For a process use бу́ду plus the imperfective: я бу́ду рабо́тать.
examples: I will be working at home.

core10.title: Asking someone to do something
core10.body: The imperative is the ты form with -й, -и or -ь: чита́й, скажи́, забу́дь; add -те to one person you say вы to, or to several.

family.title: “My” agrees with what is owned
family.body: Possessives take the gender of the thing possessed, not of the owner.

time.title: Numbers change the noun after them
time.body: 1 takes the plain form, 2–4 take a second form, and 5 and above take a third — оди́н час, два часа́, пять часо́в.

food.title: Saying what you want
food.body: хоте́ть is irregular — я хочу́, ты хо́чешь, он хо́чет, мы хоти́м — and the thing you want follows it directly.

school.title: Three ways to “study”
school.body: учи́ть is to memorise something, учи́ться is to be a student, изуча́ть is to study a subject in depth.

home.title: The ending tells you the gender
home.body: ко́мната, ку́хня, спа́льня end in -а/-я and are feminine; стол, стул, пол end in a consonant and are masculine; окно́ is neuter.

clothes.title: Adjectives take the noun’s gender
clothes.body: -ый/-ий with a masculine noun, -ая with a feminine one, -ое with a neuter one.

city.title: Places in the plural
city.body: Most take -ы/-и, but some common masculine nouns take a stressed -а́: дом → дома́, го́род → города́.

travel.title: Two verbs for “go”
travel.body: идти́ is one trip in one direction happening now; ходи́ть is going regularly or there and back.
examples: I am going to the park.
Я хожу́ в парк ка́ждый день.
I go to the park every day.

body.title: What hurts is the subject
body.body: Russian says “by me hurts the head” — the aching part is the subject, and the person comes after у: у меня́, у неё.

nature.title: Where in nature
nature.body: A few short nouns take a stressed -у́ instead of -е in the prepositional: в лесу́, в снегу́; open places take на: на мо́ре, на у́лице.

work.title: Having and not having
work.body: у меня́ есть + the plain form for having; у меня́ нет + the genitive for not having — the genitive’s first job.

animals.title: Living things take the genitive as object
animals.body: For masculine animate nouns — and all animate plurals — the accusative copies the genitive.

emotion.title: Liking is done “to” you
emotion.body: нра́виться puts the person in the dative and the thing liked in the nominative — literally “to me is pleasing”.

speech.title: Speaking a language
speech.body: говори́ть по-ру́сски uses an adverb with no case at all; the noun form needs на + prepositional.

military.title: “With” takes the instrumental
military.body: с plus the instrumental means together with — including who you are fighting or negotiating with.
examples: He is speaking with the general.

tech.title: Communicating “by” something
tech.body: по plus the dative case gives the medium something travels through.

sport.title: Playing games vs playing instruments
sport.body: игра́ть в plus the accusative for sports and games; игра́ть на plus the prepositional for instruments.

art.title: Talking about a work
art.body: о (об before a vowel) plus the prepositional case means “about”.

politics.title: Quantity words take the genitive
politics.body: After мно́го, ма́ло, ско́лько and similar words the noun goes into the genitive: plural for things you count, singular for things you measure.

medicine.title: At the doctor's
medicine.body: у plus a person means at their place — у врача́ — while в plus the prepositional is the building you are in: в больни́це.

business.title: How much does it cost?
business.body: ско́лько сто́ит plus the thing; the answer counts in roubles the way hours are counted — оди́н рубль, два рубля́, пять рубле́й.

law.title: What someone is, was, or became
law.body: After рабо́тать, стать and the past of быть, the role goes into the instrumental: юри́ст → юри́стом, судья́ → судьёй.

science.title: Doing something with something
science.body: The instrumental, with no preposition, is the field or the tool: занима́ться матема́тикой; and what someone became: стать учёным.

religion.title: Believing in
religion.body: ве́рить в plus the accusative is to believe in something; ве́рить plus the dative is to believe someone.
